t: Section 5311(c)(1)(G) of title 49, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:“(G) $11,400,000 for the period beginning on October 1, 2011, and ending on July 6, 2012.”.

fable.w: This section only amends a funding amount and time period in 49 U.S.C. 5311(c)(1)(G). It contains no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. There is no tempting opposite reading, since the text is a purely technical appropriations amendment.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely fiscal provision that amends a statute to specify a dollar amount and a time period for appropriations. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, public comment, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, hearings, or rights to sue mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Section 5311(c)(1)(G) of title 49, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:“(G) $11,400,000 for the period beginning on October 1, 2011, and ending on July 6, 2012.”

opus.w: This amendment only replaces a funding amount ($11,400,000) for the period from October 1, 2011 to July 6, 2012. It contains no process that brings outside parties into a federal decision. Section 5311 does involve grants to states and tribes, but grant funding and grant applications don't count as participation under the definition, and this text says nothing about outside involvement anyway.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning:** The only tempting reading is that 49 U.S.C. 5311 is the rural transit grant program, so states and tribes are involved somewhere. But this amendment only changes a dollar amount for a set period of time. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. Grant funding is also excluded under the definition.
